solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lightly touch, holding palm before a sexy dance

indicators.note: before places the palm-filled piece ahead of the closing letter a
holding means the first word's letters wrap round and keep the palm inside them

parts.note: to pat is to touch lightly with the hand
atap (or attap) is the nipa palm of Southeast Asia, whose leaves thatch roofs
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gives a light tap while holding a palm leaf, then launches into a provocative dance.
explanation.walkthrough: P(ATAP)AT plus A gives PATA-PATA; ATAP is a Chambers word for a palm that few solvers will know.
explanation.definitionFit: The pata-pata is a South African township dance made famous by Miriam Makeba, known for its suggestive moves.

clue.text: Passage in place where mix-up keeps Scots away

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the jumble word contains the Scots word

parts.note: pie is a printer's term for jumbled type, a mix-up
aff is Scots for off, away

explanation.surface: A corridor sits in a spot where some muddle stops Scottish visitors coming.
explanation.walkthrough: PI(AFF)E. In dressage the passage is a slow, cadenced trot, so passage here is not a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: The piaffe is the dressage movement in which a horse performs a cadenced trot on the spot without moving forward.

clue.text: Overlapping plates protect one serving of ratatouille

indicators.note: a serving is a portion, so only part of the dish's name is taken

parts.note: the letters sit in the middle of the vegetable stew's name

explanation.surface: Stacked dishes keep one portion of vegetable stew covered.
explanation.walkthrough: The plates are not crockery but bony armour; the answer is an animal so protected.
explanation.definitionFit: The tatou is the armadillo, whose body is shielded by overlapping bony plates.

clue.text: Cordial individual almost finished eating chip

indicators.note: eating means taking inside, so the shortened word swallows the chip
almost finished means the word stops just short of its last letter

parts.note: a person is an individual
IC is an integrated circuit, a silicon chip

explanation.surface: A friendly person, nearly done with a meal, is munching a chip.
explanation.walkthrough: Cordial looks like an adjective for the friendly person, but it is a noun naming a sweet drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Persico is a liqueur flavoured with the kernels of peaches or apricots, a sweet alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Past upturns claimed by sources of finance with credit on thin ice

indicators.note: with adds the credit piece alongside the rest

parts.note: on tick is British slang for on credit

indicators.note: claimed by means taken in by, so the reversed piece goes inside the moneylenders

parts.note: lenders provide money

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: by means past, as in walking by

explanation.surface: Banks swallowed past rises while lending on credit, putting them on thin ice.
explanation.walkthrough: TICK plus L(YB)ENDERS. Thin ice is not a metaphor here but the literal thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickly-benders is a New England name for thin ice that bends under a skater, or the game of running over it.

clue.text: Tiny insect in lettuce with thick sauce dressing that's sent back

indicators.note: sent back means the whole assembled piece is read in the opposite direction
a dressing goes over and around food, so the sauce wraps round the salad leaf

parts.note: a dip is a thick sauce for dunking
cos is a variety of lettuce, romaine in the US

explanation.surface: A diner finds a minute bug in a salad drenched in a heavy dressing and returns the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: DI(COS)P read backwards gives PSOCID.
explanation.definitionFit: Psocids are booklice and barklice, very small soft-bodied insects of the order Psocoptera.

clue.text: Small boat store in which everything must go

indicators.note: in which says the following word goes inside the shop
must go reads as must go in, completing the instruction to insert

parts.note: a shop is a store
all means everything

explanation.surface: A dinghy is on offer at a closing-down sale where everything must go.
explanation.walkthrough: Everything must go is a familiar clearance-sale slogan; SH(ALL)OP.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallop is a light open boat, propelled by oars or a sail, used in shallow waters.

clue.text: Something to drive apart from rise of insidious insecticides

parts.note: a car is driven
bar means except, apart from

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: sly means insidious, cunning

explanation.surface: Apart from a vehicle, an insidious rise in pesticide use is the worry.
explanation.walkthrough: Apart from looks like a separator, but here it is BAR, as in all bar one.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbaryl is a carbamate chemical widely sprayed to kill garden and farm pests.

clue.text: Gas money in the US, superior to your old pounds

indicators.note: in a down clue superior means placed above, so the coin sits on top

parts.note: a dime is a US ten-cent coin
thy is the archaic form of your
L, from Latin libra, stands for pounds

explanation.surface: An American spending on gas, rich enough to look down on your former sterling.
explanation.walkthrough: Gas suggests US petrol money, but it is the chemical; dimethyl is another name for ethane.
explanation.definitionFit: Dimethyl is an old name for ethane, a colourless flammable gas made of two methyl groups.

clue.text: Exhausted again, chesty? Nothing short of bacterial disease

indicators.note: exhausted means emptied out, so only the shell of the word again survives

parts.note: the word emptied of its middle leaves its first and last letters

indicators.note: short means lacking, so the word for chesty goes without the letter for nothing

parts.note: thoracic means of the chest
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A patient, worn out once more and with a bad chest, fears it is nothing less than a bacterial infection.
explanation.walkthrough: Exhausted reads as tired, but here it means emptied, as a mine is exhausted of its contents.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthracic is the adjective from anthrax, the infection caused by Bacillus anthracis.

clue.text: Antibiotic agents to curb disease, checking how hysterical, cold and hot

indicators.note: to curb is to restrain, holding something in, so the agents enclose the disease

parts.note: the CIA is the US agency whose staff are agents

indicators.note: checking means stopping or holding in, so the disease word holds the laughter

parts.note: pox is a disease
ROFL, rolling on the floor laughing, is internet shorthand for finding something hysterical
C is the tap marking for cold
in means fashionable, hot

explanation.surface: Health officials move to contain an outbreak, monitoring how feverish the patients run between chills and heat.
explanation.walkthrough: CI(P(ROFL)OX)A, then C and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciprofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone drug that kills bacteria, widely prescribed for infections.

clue.text: Stoker possibly behind a disused copper

indicators.note: behind places the novelist's first name after the single letter that follows

parts.note: taken as written
Bram Stoker wrote Dracula; possibly flags the first name as one example of a Stoker

explanation.surface: It reads like a fireman shovelling coal on a ship standing behind an old police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: A stoker feeds a furnace and a copper is a policeman, but here Stoker is the author and copper is a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Abram is an obsolete form of auburn, an old word for a reddish-brown, copper-coloured hue of hair.

clue.text: Cornish river skirts capitals and island area of upper Red Lane

indicators.note: to skirt is to run round the edge, so the river's letters go round the rest

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall reaching the sea at Falmouth
UC is the printer's abbreviation for upper case, capital letters
I is the standard abbreviation for island
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A Cornish river flows round towns and an island in the higher reaches of some lane.
explanation.walkthrough: The red lane is a jocular old name for the throat; FA(UC I A)L gives FAUCIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Faucial means relating to the fauces, the passage at the back of the mouth leading into the throat.

clue.text: Soldier only lightly armed: hide or bombard with a stone?

parts.note: pelt means both an animal's hide and to bombard with missiles
taken as written
st is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

explanation.surface: A poorly equipped fighter wonders whether to take cover or hurl rocks at the enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses of one word meet in the first piece, and stone is the weight, not a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A peltast was an ancient Greek light infantryman carrying javelins and a small crescent shield called a pelta.

clue.text: After letter, Moody Blues initially support backing tracks involving extremely heavy rock

indicators.note: after puts the Greek letter first, with everything else following it

parts.note: rho is the Greek letter R

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each word of the band's name

parts.note: the first letters of the band's two words

indicators.note: involving means wrapping up, so the combined piece encloses the extreme letters
backing means going backwards, so the word for support is read the other way

parts.note: a prop is a support
RY is the abbreviation for railway, tracks

indicators.note: extremely means taking only the extremes, the first and last letters of heavy

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A record review: after a letter, the Moody Blues get backing tracks with some heavy rock.
explanation.walkthrough: Heavy, tracks and rock all pull towards music, but rock is the stone and tracks are railway lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhomb-porphyry is an igneous stone with rhomb-shaped feldspar crystals, found notably around Oslo.

clue.text: Bloody fluid used as supplement, forgetting every day remains

indicators.note: D stands for day, and forgetting every one means removing every such letter

parts.note: red is the colour of blood
a fluid is a liquid
something added is used as a supplement

explanation.surface: A blood product is given as a supplement, but something has been left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: RED LIQUID ADDED with all four Ds removed leaves RELIQUIAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Reliquiae is a Latin plural for leftover things, especially fossil or organic relics.

clue.text: More than one slight burn in the end, covered with hot drinks when head is lowered

indicators.note: covered with means wrapped by, so the single letter sits inside the drinks
the leading letter drops down within its word, a rearrangement of its letters

parts.note: coffees are hot drinks

indicators.note: in the end asks for the final letter of burn only

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Several small injuries: a scald at last, from hot drinks spilt when someone's head drooped.
explanation.walkthrough: COFFEES with its C moved down becomes OFFECES, and N goes inside; slight is a noun, an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Offences are insults or affronts, and a slight is an act that gives offence.

clue.text: Characters that may be uniquely placed to reveal sinful bastard

parts.words: Characters that may be uniquely placed to reveal sinful
parts.note: surface reading: certain people are in a unique position to expose wrongdoing

parts.words: Characters that may be uniquely placed
parts.note: setter's reading: the answer is spelt only with the six letters of sinful, and each letter used once and rearranged reveals that word

explanation.surface: Certain people are uniquely placed to expose a wicked scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Characters means letters, not people: the Latin phrase repeats F, I, L, U, S and N, which taken once each spell sinful.
explanation.definitionFit: Filius nullius is Latin for son of nobody, the legal term for an illegitimate child.

clue.text: Once abundant in America, robe set off uniform

indicators.note: in places the following pieces inside the country's letters

parts.note: US is the United States

indicators.note: set off means disturbed or launched, so the garment's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Once plentiful in America, a robe set off a uniform nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: U(BERO U)S; once marks the definition as an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Uberous is an obsolete adjective meaning fruitful or copious, from Latin uber, fertile.

clue.text: Aftersales service shows the reverse of such intemperance

indicators.note: the reverse means the visible letters are read backwards
shows means displays, so the letters are on view inside the phrase

parts.note: these letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Customer care after a purchase proves the opposite of excess.
explanation.walkthrough: Such points back to the French-looking aftersales phrase, hinting at a French word for intemperance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivresse is French for drunkenness, the state of being intoxicated, used in English for exhilaration.

clue.text: Letter from scripture conveying female ancestor's spiritual insights

indicators.note: conveying means carrying along, so the letter is followed by the rest

parts.note: J is the scholars' label for the Yahwist source of the books of Moses
a nana is a grandmother, with the possessive s

explanation.surface: A letter from the Bible carries a grandmother's religious wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: Letter suggests an epistle, but it is one letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Jnana is the Hindu term for knowledge gained through meditation, a path to spiritual liberation.

clue.text: Robespierre's tied behind the neck to line up for execution

definitions.meaning: first meaning: French for in a pigtail, with Robespierre standing for the French language
second meaning: in computing, to place a job in a waiting list to be run

explanation.surface: A revolutionary's hair is bound back as victims are marched towards the guillotine.
explanation.walkthrough: Execution suggests the Terror, but the second sense is a computer running tasks in order.
explanation.definitionFit: In computing, a job is put at the back of a waiting list before the processor runs it.

clue.text: Nothing to cover cost of travel to west: coin no longer used

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means reading right to left
to cover is to go round, so the word for nothing encloses the travel cost

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing
a fare is the price of a journey

explanation.surface: Someone has nothing to pay for a trip westward, as the old money has gone out of use.
explanation.walkthrough: NI(FARE)X reversed gives XERAFIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The xerafin was a silver coin of Portuguese India, long since withdrawn from circulation.

clue.text: Operetta composer, he was most productive around periphery

indicators.note: around means the abbreviation for flourished goes round the edge word

parts.note: fl, floruit, marks when someone flourished
a rim is a periphery

explanation.surface: A light-opera writer had his most fruitful years on the fringes.
explanation.walkthrough: F(RIM)L; floruit dates the peak of a career.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Friml wrote Rose-Marie and The Vagabond King, popular stage operettas of the 1920s.

clue.text: Greeting among Canadians, maybe Ontarians primarily?

definitions.text: Greeting among Canadians, maybe Ontarians primarily?

indicators.note: among puts the greeting inside the letters for the Canadians

parts.note: CM are the post-nominal letters of a Member of the Order of Canada
hi is a greeting

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of the following word only

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A greeting heard among Canadians, perhaps mainly from people in Ontario.
explanation.walkthrough: C(HI)M plus O; the whole clue also describes the word, with the question mark hedging the Ontario part.
explanation.definitionFit: Chimo is an Inuit salutation adopted in Canadian English as a friendly hello or toast.

clue.text: Financial centre in period of activity for Brexit, say

indicators.note: in places the financial district's letters inside the stretch of activity

parts.note: a session is a period devoted to some activity
EC is the postcode of the City of London, Britain's financial centre

explanation.surface: The City of London busy during a parliamentary sitting about Brexit.
explanation.walkthrough: S(EC)ESSION; say marks Brexit as one example, Britain leaving the European Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Brexit was the United Kingdom's withdrawal from the European Union, a breakaway from a political union.

clue.text: Wanting love, certain people take advantage of abandoned hole in wall

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the word for certain people goes without the letter for love

parts.note: some means certain people, not all
love is zero in tennis, O
to use someone is to take advantage of them

explanation.surface: Loveless people exploit a gap left in a deserted wall.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is zero in tennis scoring, which is why it removes a single O.
explanation.definitionFit: Smeuse is a dialect word for a gap in a hedge or wall worn through by a hare or other small animal.

clue.text: Monkey nut? We want to hear about it!

parts.note: in printing an en is called a nut, to tell it apart from an em, a mutton

parts.words: We want to hear about it!
parts.note: the phrase a curious audience says: tell us

explanation.surface: Someone mentions a monkey nut and listeners eagerly ask for the story.
explanation.walkthrough: Monkey nut, a peanut, is a false phrase: monkey is the definition and nut is the printer's word for an en space.
explanation.definitionFit: The entellus is the Hanuman langur, a sacred grey monkey of India.
